headlines.description: A surprising new study found that people who sleep near their dogs don’t experience disrupted sleep. If anything we humans are the ones disturbing our dogs’ sleep.

headlines.title: Tips for Taking Better Care of Your Mental Well-Being
headlines.description: As the year comes to an end and life gets busier, it can be difficult to keep a consistent routine and find time to take care of both your physical and mental health. headlines.title: Do Viral Health Claims About Living Longer Actually Work?
headlines.description: Viral health trends across social media claim to increase both stamina and longevity, but do they really work? TODAY medical contributor Dr. Natalie Azar joins TODAY to differentiate fact from fiction by breaking down social media health claims, from cold plunges and cortisol levels to wearable trackers and more.

headlines.title: Adam Grant on Connecting With People With 3 Types of Bonds
headlines.description: Bestselling author and organizational psychologist Adam Grant joins TODAY to share ideas to form bonds with others from his new book “Vibe: The Secrets of Strong Connections in a Lonely World.” Grant breaks down how people categorize friends into three different types of bonds, why we should skip small talk when sparking connections, and how to sustain the connections in our lives.

headlines.title: How This Teen's Health Journey Shaped Her Passion for Softball
headlines.description: After developing an unprecedented and progressive spinal curvature, known, 10-year-old Macie Perna feared her love for playing softball may be lost forever. But, a life-changing operation at Shriners Children's Philadelphia called Vertebral Body Tethering, or VBT, hit those fears out of the park. Just six weeks later, Perna was back on the field stronger than ever before. Now, at 16, she has no restrictions and big dreams.
